      "title": "Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce refresh path",
      "body": "The new code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this module neither imports nor declares `prisma`. This fails TypeScript checking and, if checking is bypassed, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce operations even when credential sharing is disabled."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",

      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result",
      "body": "`parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `{ success: true, data: ... }` wrapper, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Saving that wrapper as `credential.key` removes the token fields from the root of the stored credentials. This happens even with sharing disabled, so the next service initialization cannot load the Google credentials correctly. Persist the result's `data` instead."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Use real schema fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas",
      "body": "Both computed property names evaluate to the literal string `[object Object]`; they do not define arbitrary numeric or optional properties. Since Zod objects strip unknown fields by default, a normal sync response loses its expiry, refresh token, and other metadata. For example, Zoom then calculates its new expiry from an undefined `expires_in`, producing NaN. Define and preserve the actual response fields, including the expiry information consumed by each adapter."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 15,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Adapt fetch responses for callers that expect SDK or Axios results",
      "body": "The sync branch returns a raw fetch `Response`, but Google, Zoho CRM, and Bigin read `.data` from the result, while HubSpot treats the result itself as a parsed token object. A fetch Response has none of those token properties, regardless of the JSON returned by the endpoint. Consequently, successful sync requests throw on undefined fields or fail to install the returned tokens. Decode and adapt the response at these callers, with an explicit return contract rather than `any`."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts",
      "line": 25,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder",
      "body": "This fallback runs for native provider responses as well as shared credentials. Office 365 explicitly permits a refresh response without a new `refresh_token`; its caller previously retained the existing token when merging the response. The helper now inserts the literal `refresh_token`, which overwrites that valid token in the database and causes the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not rotate it."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoho-bigin/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 93,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Pass the credential owner's user ID to Bigin credential sync",
      "body": "The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a user ID, but this call supplies the credential row's ID. The helper sends that value as `calcomUserId`, so whenever these independent IDs differ it requests a nonexistent or different user's integration. It also incorrectly routes team credentials through user sync because their credential IDs are non-null. Pass `credential.userId` separately from the ID used for database updates."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts",
      "line": 8,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "security",
      "title": "Authenticate outbound credential-refresh requests",
      "body": "The token-retrieval request sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no shared-secret header, signature, or other authentication. An externally reachable parent endpoint cannot distinguish this request from an arbitrary caller supplying the same identifiers: it must either reject these calls or risk exposing users' third-party access tokens. Add an explicit server-to-server authentication mechanism to the refresh protocol."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/zoomvideo/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 92,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Send Zoom's app slug rather than its directory name",
      "body": "This sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the parent store, but Zoom is installed with `appId: \"zoom\"` and the credential webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent store keyed by that same slug cannot match the refresh request to the synced Zoom credential. Use `zoom`, consistently with installation and webhook requests."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 75,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint",
      "body": "Unlike the other modified integrations, Salesforce always posts directly to the provider and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential sharing therefore has no effect on where Salesforce obtains tokens. Credentials whose refresh tokens are managed only by the parent store fail this request instead of using the configured sync endpoint, defeating the new feature for Salesforce."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/webex/lib/VideoApiAdapter.ts",
      "line": 62,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Accept the minimal sync response in the Webex adapter",
      "body": "The new sync helper documents a response containing only the access token and expiry, but Webex still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token lifetime. A successful response following the sync contract is therefore rejected as invalid when the access token expires. Add sync-specific decoding and retain the existing provider metadata rather than requiring native refresh-response fields."
    },
    {
      "file": "packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts",
      "line": 67,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "Decode shared Lark tokens without requiring a native response envelope",
      "body": "The sync response is passed directly to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>` and then read through `data.data`, including refresh-token lifetime fields. The helper's documented access-token-and-expiry response has neither Lark's `code`/`data` envelope nor that refresh-token metadata, so a valid shared-token response cannot refresh this integration. Handle the sync response separately from Lark's native refresh response."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 78,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Clear the invalid flag when replacing repaired credentials",
      "body": "Google, Zoom, and Webex can mark a credential `invalid: true` after an unrecoverable authentication failure. If the user reconnects in the parent application and sends fresh keys through this webhook, the update changes only `key`, leaving the same row marked invalid. The webhook reports success without restoring the connection. Clear the invalid flag when accepting valid replacement credentials."
    },
    {
      "file": "apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts",
      "line": 83,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "concurrency",
      "title": "Make initial credential synchronization idempotent under concurrency",
      "body": "The lookup and creation are separate operations with no serialization or stable upsert key. Two simultaneous deliveries for a user/app with no existing credential can both observe no row and both create one. Subsequent webhook updates modify only the first matching row, leaving the duplicate with stale tokens. Serialize creation for the logical credential or introduce an idempotent identity that can be atomically upserted."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Import Prisma before using it in the Salesforce refresh path
findings.body: The new code calls `prisma.credential.update`, but this module neither imports nor declares `prisma`. This fails TypeScript checking and, if checking is bypassed, throws a ReferenceError after a successful token refresh, preventing Salesforce operations even when credential sharing is disabled.

findings.title: Persist the parsed Google credentials, not the safeParse result
findings.body: `parseRefreshTokenResponse` returns a `{ success: true, data: ... }` wrapper, whereas the previous `googleCredentialSchema.parse` returned the credentials themselves. Saving that wrapper as `credential.key` removes the token fields from the root of the stored credentials. This happens even with sharing disabled, so the next service initialization cannot load the Google credentials correctly. Persist the result's `data` instead.

findings.title: Use real schema fields instead of stringifying Zod schemas
findings.body: Both computed property names evaluate to the literal string `[object Object]`; they do not define arbitrary numeric or optional properties. Since Zod objects strip unknown fields by default, a normal sync response loses its expiry, refresh token, and other metadata. For example, Zoom then calculates its new expiry from an undefined `expires_in`, producing NaN. Define and preserve the actual response fields, including the expiry information consumed by each adapter.

findings.title: Adapt fetch responses for callers that expect SDK or Axios results
findings.body: The sync branch returns a raw fetch `Response`, but Google, Zoho CRM, and Bigin read `.data` from the result, while HubSpot treats the result itself as a parsed token object. A fetch Response has none of those token properties, regardless of the JSON returned by the endpoint. Consequently, successful sync requests throw on undefined fields or fail to install the returned tokens. Decode and adapt the response at these callers, with an explicit return contract rather than `any`.

findings.title: Do not replace an existing refresh token with a placeholder
findings.body: This fallback runs for native provider responses as well as shared credentials. Office 365 explicitly permits a refresh response without a new `refresh_token`; its caller previously retained the existing token when merging the response. The helper now inserts the literal `refresh_token`, which overwrites that valid token in the database and causes the next refresh to fail. Preserve the existing refresh token when the provider does not rotate it.

findings.title: Pass the credential owner's user ID to Bigin credential sync
findings.body: The third argument to `refreshOAuthTokens` is a user ID, but this call supplies the credential row's ID. The helper sends that value as `calcomUserId`, so whenever these independent IDs differ it requests a nonexistent or different user's integration. It also incorrectly routes team credentials through user sync because their credential IDs are non-null. Pass `credential.userId` separately from the ID used for database updates.

findings.title: Authenticate outbound credential-refresh requests
findings.body: The token-retrieval request sends only `calcomUserId` and `appSlug`, with no shared-secret header, signature, or other authentication. An externally reachable parent endpoint cannot distinguish this request from an arbitrary caller supplying the same identifiers: it must either reject these calls or risk exposing users' third-party access tokens. Add an explicit server-to-server authentication mechanism to the refresh protocol.

findings.title: Send Zoom's app slug rather than its directory name
findings.body: This sends `appSlug=zoomvideo` to the parent store, but Zoom is installed with `appId: "zoom"` and the credential webhook identifies apps by their database slug. A parent store keyed by that same slug cannot match the refresh request to the synced Zoom credential. Use `zoom`, consistently with installation and webhook requests.

findings.title: Route Salesforce refreshes through the configured sync endpoint
findings.body: Unlike the other modified integrations, Salesforce always posts directly to the provider and never calls `refreshOAuthTokens`. Enabling credential sharing therefore has no effect on where Salesforce obtains tokens. Credentials whose refresh tokens are managed only by the parent store fail this request instead of using the configured sync endpoint, defeating the new feature for Salesforce.

findings.title: Accept the minimal sync response in the Webex adapter
findings.body: The new sync helper documents a response containing only the access token and expiry, but Webex still validates that response with `webexRefreshedTokenSchema`, which requires scope, token type, refresh token, and refresh-token lifetime. A successful response following the sync contract is therefore rejected as invalid when the access token expires. Add sync-specific decoding and retain the existing provider metadata rather than requiring native refresh-response fields.

findings.title: Decode shared Lark tokens without requiring a native response envelope
findings.body: The sync response is passed directly to `handleLarkError<RefreshTokenResp>` and then read through `data.data`, including refresh-token lifetime fields. The helper's documented access-token-and-expiry response has neither Lark's `code`/`data` envelope nor that refresh-token metadata, so a valid shared-token response cannot refresh this integration. Handle the sync response separately from Lark's native refresh response.

findings.title: Clear the invalid flag when replacing repaired credentials

findings.title: Make initial credential synchronization idempotent under concurrency

Two simultaneous deliveries for a user/app with no existing credential can both observe no row and both create one. Subsequent webhook updates modify only the first matching row, leaving the duplicate with stale tokens. Serialize creation for the logical credential or introduce an idempotent identity that can be atomically upserted.
